subject: EOQ synthesis and prioritization — need final OKR narratives for QBR pack
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: qbr-support@redwood-corp.com
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: EOQ synthesis and prioritization — need final OKR narratives for QBR pack

Team —

Attached is my pass at a concise EOQ synthesis (EOQ_scoring_bandings_v3.xlsx) plus the one-pager draft we’ll use in the executive QBR (QBR_onepager_deltas.pdf). High level asks:

- Please review the bandings column and the short narrative bullets for each Objective. I tried to compress to the three-line rationale we agreed on.
- Two objectives need explicit evidence before I lock the final score: Objective 2 (Dedicated capacity efficiency) and Objective 5 (Reduce inference cost for low-latency workloads).
- I want final language + sign-off by 09:00 PT tomorrow so SLT pack can be assembled.

Notes on approach I used: I avoided granular metric-by-metric redlines and instead proposed a +/0/- band where + = exceeds, 0 = met, - = missed. The narrative column ties to customer anecdotes or infra telemetry where possible.

If you disagree with a banding, call it out inline in the sheet and add a one-line correction in the reply thread with the evidence pointer (link to logs, eval, or customer quote).

Two quick thoughts for the QBR: emphasize routing + caching wins as durable platform differentiation; minimize technology nomenclature in the exec one-pager.

Thanks —
Vivek

[Attachment: EOQ_scoring_bandings_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 310KB)]
[Attachment: QBR_onepager_deltas.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EOQ synthesis and prioritization — need final OKR narratives for QBR pack

Vivek — thanks, good distillation. A few inline items:

- Objective 1 (Adoption of Redwood API): band stays at +. We have the HubSpot conversion timestamps and three new logos that closed late March. See sheet tab "Adoption_evidence" (rows 4-9).
- Objective 2 (Dedicated capacity efficiency): I think this is a 0, not +. We saw a regression in GPU utilization in the last fortnight because of an unanticipated workload with long context windows; allocation overhead offset some batching gains. I added a short note and linked the infra trace (link in the sheet).
- For the one-pager language, please prefer "throughput and latency economics" rather than internal terms like "continuous KV caching" — execs respond better to economics-first framing.

I’m attaching the customer quote that supports Objective 1 win (short snippet).

Laura

[Attachment: customer_quote_acme_excerpt.txt (txt, 1.2KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 07:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EOQ synthesis and prioritization — need final OKR narratives for QBR pack

Morning — quick read and two proposals: 

1) Evidence packaging: For Objective 5 (reduce inference cost for low-latency workloads), I can surface the A/B test from Feb that shows 12% unit-cost reduction when we applied new batching thresholds. I uploaded a short slide to the Drive link (Drive: EOQPack/Obj5 A-B slides).

2) Narrative tone: for objectives where progress was mixed, can we add a single "risk/mitigation" bullet? It helps the board see the plan instead of just a score. Example for Obj2: "Risk: allocation mismatch for long-context; Mitigation: revised autoscale policy baseline & two-week pilot on dedicated pools."

Also, I'm neutral on banding for Obj2 — Laura's infra notes are convincing; if Jonas has telemetry that flips the sign, we should use it.

—Marissa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EOQ synthesis and prioritization — need final OKR narratives for QBR pack

Folks —

I dug into the GPU utilization traces Laura referenced. Two clarifications:

- The regression coincides with a single customer experiment that increased median context length ~3x for a subset of requests between Mar 10–20. Once that experiment ended utilization normalized. I added the trace pointers under "Obj2_infra" in the sheet.
- Because the root cause is a bounded experiment the band could be + but with an asterisk in the narrative: "+ (see infra note: temporary utilization anomaly from a customer experiment)".

If the committee prefers a conservative posture, a 0 is reasonable; I support marking + with the mitigation bullet Marissa suggested.

Jonas

Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EOQ synthesis and prioritization — need final OKR narratives for QBR pack

Thanks all — helpful. Quick decisions: 

- Obj2: mark as + with an inline parenthetical explaining the temporary customer experiment and link to the infra trace. Marissa, please add the risk/mitigation bullet.
- Obj5: Marissa, please drop the Feb A/B slide into the scoring sheet and we’ll cite that in the one-pager; that should move the band to +.
- Laura: update the one-pager language to the economics-first phrasing and trim the technology sentence as suggested.

I’ll incorporate these changes and produce the final SLT pack by 14:00 PT (I’ll send the assembled PDF to qbr-support and Elena for review). If anyone expects to push back after 09:00 PT, flag it here now.

Vivek
